ops.body:
**Concrete driver found, 2026-08-31** — this is no longer a hypothetical API gap. It is what stops cc-squash's integration suite from being safe to run.

`go/internal/integration/coldstart_test.go` creates a temp HOME, but daemonkit resolves its state root through the **passwd database and ignores HOME**, so the harness must export `DAEMONKIT_HOME` to every process it spawns. That works for direct child processes — and is not enough, because the harness drives `ccs url`, which converges through launchd, and **launchd starts the agent from the rendered plist**. `daemonkit.Daemon` has no `Env` field, so the plist cannot carry `DAEMONKIT_HOME`, and the launchd-started daemon comes up in the developer's real home.

**This was observed, not reasoned about.** A guarded run fingerprinted the passwd home before and after and caught the mutation:

    the harness mutated the real installation at /Users/yasyf/.daemonkit/a/com.yasyf.cc-squash.daemon
    before: absent
    after:  daemon.records ...

and the daemon's own log confirmed `socket=/Users/yasyf/.daemonkit/...`. The directory that run created was moved to Trash; `~/.cc-squash` was proven untouched by the same fingerprint.

**Consequence, landed in cc-squash `4d04c77`:** `TestColdStartTwoProcess` now `t.Skip`s with that exact reason rather than serving out of the real installation, behind three guards (a passwd-home fingerprint, a refusal to run while the real LaunchAgent is bootstrapped — launchd's domain is per-user, so `DAEMONKIT_HOME` cannot isolate a label — and a positive assert that every path is under the temp root). The suite is build-tagged, so it was always opt-in; it is now opt-in **and** safe, instead of opt-in and quietly destructive.

**What an `Env` field would unblock**, all currently uncovered in cc-squash: cold start, warm reuse, respawn, and real-home isolation; plus two findings an adversarial pass raised that have no in-process home — a live `Client.Health` round trip (the control lane is codesign-gated on `Requirement{TeamID: SXKCTF23Q2}`, so an unsigned test binary cannot attach, and a self-exec child does not lift that because the gate is codesign-based, not process-relationship-based), and driving `Ctx.Reclaimed` from a genuinely orphaned child record rather than injecting it.

Note the label caveat: even with `Env`, launchd's domain is per-user, so two concurrent runs of a suite that bootstraps the same label still collide. An isolated run needs a per-run label as well as a per-run home.
